titre_exercice: Essay - Topic 3 : la lettre persuasive à un proche
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Topic 3**

Your parents want you to be a pilot. But you are interested in teaching. Discuss with your parents and convince them that teaching is the best profession.

questions.enonce_markdown: **Topic 3.** Write a letter to your parents explaining why you prefer teaching to becoming a pilot, and convince them that teaching is the best profession for you. *(180 to 220 words)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Une lettre adressée à ses propres parents pour défendre un choix personnel commence par reconnaître leur point de vue avec respect (jamais par une opposition frontale), avant d'avancer ses propres arguments et de conclure par une demande claire de soutien.

**Modèle de la lettre persuasive à un proche (180 à 220 mots) :**

Dear Mum and Dad,

I know you have always dreamed of seeing me become a pilot, flying planes across the world, and I am grateful for the ambition you hold for my future. However, after much reflection, I have discovered that my true passion lies in teaching, not aviation.

Since my early years in secondary school, I have always enjoyed explaining difficult lessons to my classmates and watching their faces light up once they finally understand a notion that once confused them. That feeling of helping someone grow means more to me than any other career could.

Teaching is also a noble and necessary profession. Every pilot, every doctor, every engineer you can think of first learned to read, write and reason because a teacher took the time to guide them. Without teachers, no other profession, including piloting, would even exist.

Furthermore, becoming a teacher does not mean a life of hardship. With dedication, a teacher can rise to become a school principal, an inspector, or even a university lecturer, building a stable and respected career.

Dear parents, please trust my judgment and support me on this path. I promise to work hard and become a teacher you will be proud of, just as you would have been proud of a pilot.

### Piège à éviter
Rejeter d'emblée le souhait des parents (« I will never be a pilot ») sans d'abord reconnaître leur intention bienveillante donne un ton conflictuel qui dessert l'argumentation, même si les arguments qui suivent sont solides.

### Conseil
Ouvre toujours ce type de lettre par une reconnaissance sincère de l'intention des parents avant d'exposer ton propre choix : cela installe un ton respectueux qui rend tes arguments suivants plus recevables.
